# `Q-18-1` — Engine Returned an Unreadable Result

> An execution engine finished, but the result it handed back was not
> in the shape Quarto expects, so the render could not continue.

## What this means

When a document has executable code cells, Quarto hands the document to
an execution engine (knitr for R, jupyter for Python and other kernels,
or an engine extension). The engine runs the cells and returns a
structured result: the markdown with cell outputs spliced in, plus
supporting files, header includes, and similar bookkeeping.

This error means the engine ran and returned *something*, but Quarto
could not read one of those fields. The message names the field (for
example `includes.include-in-header`) and what was wrong with it.

**This is not a problem with your document.** The engine and the code
that reads its result both ship with Quarto; a mismatch between them is
a bug in Quarto's integration with that engine.

## Why this happens

- A Quarto release changed one side of the engine protocol without the
  other. (The first instance of this code: knitr reports header
  includes as a list of files, and an early Quarto 2 expected a single
  file, so any R output that attached an HTML dependency — an
  htmlwidget such as `reactable` or `DT` — failed to render.)
- A newer or older engine package than the one Quarto was tested with
  (for example an unusual `knitr` or `rmarkdown` version) writes a field
  in a shape Quarto has not seen.

## How to fix

There is nothing to change in your document. Please report the problem:

1. Open an issue at <https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues>.
2. Include the full error text — it names the field that could not be
   read.
3. Attach the preserved result file. The message names its path; Quarto
   keeps the engine's raw output on disk when this error fires, so the
   exact bytes the engine produced can be inspected.
4. Mention the engine and its version (for knitr, the output of
   `packageVersion("knitr")` and `packageVersion("rmarkdown")` in R).

If you are blocked, check whether the cell that triggers the failure can
be narrowed: for knitr, the trigger is usually the first cell whose
output carries an HTML dependency.
